# terradish ![terradish logo](reference/figures/terradish-sticker.png)

| CI | CRAN | License | Archive |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| [![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/wpeterman/terradish/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wpeterman/terradish/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml) | [![CRAN status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/terradish)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=terradish) | [![License: BSD 3-Clause](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-BSD_3--Clause-blue.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/BSD-3-Clause) | [![DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/DOI/10.5281/zenodo.21225711.svg)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21225711) |

## Overview

terradish estimates landscape conductance surfaces from genetic data by
maximum likelihood on a raster graph. It fits log-linear conductance
models and can optionally estimate each covariate’s Gaussian smoothing
scale and spline shape.

Models fit pairwise genetic distances through the MLPE likelihood, or
allele-frequency covariance and squared distances derived from it
through a Wishart likelihood on site contrasts. Both families accept the
same pairwise environmental covariates alongside resistance. Exact
sparse Cholesky and algebraic multigrid solvers handle large rasters.
Fixed-domain spatial cross-validation compares conductance formulas.

Estimated coefficients describe relative conductance and are conditional
on the measurement-model terms. They do not directly estimate movement,
migration, or causal landscape effects. For Wishart likelihoods, the
user-supplied information parameter `nu` controls inferential precision.
Using the SNP count overstated information by roughly an order of
magnitude in the package’s forward-time validation experiments.

## Citation

To cite terradish or acknowledge its use, run `citation("terradish")`
for the current reference and a BibTeX entry. The archived releases
share the DOI
[10.5281/zenodo.21225711](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21225711).

Fitting one parameterized conductance surface to genetic data, in place
of regressing on separate resistance distances, follows Peterman and
Pope (2021), [doi:10.1111/mec.15716](https://doi.org/10.1111/mec.15716).

## Installation

There are two ways to install terradish:

``` r

# Get the released version from CRAN
install.packages("terradish")

# Alternatively, install the development version from GitHub
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("wpeterman/terradish")
```

terradish requires the companion package landgraph, version 0.0.3 or
later. Both routes install it from CRAN automatically.

## Using terradish

The full documentation, with every guide and help page, is at
<https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/>.

A terradish analysis has three steps: build a raster graph from
covariates and sampling locations with
[`conductance_surface()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/conductance_surface.md),
fit a conductance model to a genetic response with
[`terradish()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish.md),
and then check, compare, and map the fit.

### Quick start

``` r

library(terradish)
library(terra)
data(melip)

# Unwrap the portable example data and standardize each raster layer.
altitude <- terra::unwrap(melip.altitude)
forestcover <- terra::unwrap(melip.forestcover)
sites <- terra::unwrap(melip.coords)
covariates <- c(altitude, forestcover)
names(covariates) <- c("altitude", "forestcover")
covariates <- scale_covariates(covariates)

# A few sites fall in the same raster cell. Keep one site per cell so that
# each graph vertex holds one sampled population.
keep <- !duplicated(terra::cellFromXY(covariates, terra::crds(sites)))
sites <- sites[keep]
Fst <- melip.Fst[keep, keep]
graph <- conductance_surface(covariates, sites)  # eight neighbors by default

# MLPE accounts for shared sampling sites among pairwise genetic distances.
fit <- terradish(Fst ~ forestcover + altitude, graph,
                 measurement_model = mlpe)
fit$convergence
summary(fit)
coef(fit)
confint(fit)
vcov(fit)
plot(fit, type = "surface", data = graph)
plot(fit, type = "fit")
```

Check convergence before interpreting the surface. Code 0 meets the
stopping rule; code 1 reaches the iteration limit; code 2 reports a
stall or failed line search. Also inspect `fit$fit$subproblem` for
nuisance optimization. Numerical convergence does not establish model
adequacy.

## Interpreting estimates

For a standardized linear covariate, `exp(coef(fit))` is the conductance
multiplier for a one-standard-deviation increase, holding other terms
fixed. A common conductance scale is absorbed by the measurement model’s
resistance coefficient, so absolute conductance is unidentified.

Gaussian `sigma` describes raster smoothing in map units. The smoothed
layer is re-standardized at every candidate sigma, so its coefficient is
per standard deviation of that layer. The half-cell lower bound still
smooths, and the upper bound is limited by the retained kernel window.
Dispersal averaging can favor positive scales without a separate
ecological scale of effect. Use
[`gaussian_scale_summary()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/gaussian_scale_summary.md),
`summary(fit)$sigma_table`, and
[`gaussian_scale_profile()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/gaussian_scale_profile.md)
to examine units, bounds, and uncertainty.

Spline models are unpenalized regression splines with fixed degrees of
freedom. Their centered bases and knots are retained for prediction.
`summary(fit)$spline_monotonicity` describes shape over the focal-site
covariate range. Tails outside that range are poorly identified.

| Response | Measurement model | Main requirement |
|----|----|----|
| Pairwise genetic distances, including ratio-estimator FST | `mlpe` or `leastsquares` | A defensible mean structure; MLPE models shared-site correlation |
| Allele-frequency covariance | `wishart_covariance` | Coherent covariance and explicit effective information |
| Squared distances derived from covariance | `generalized_wishart` | Admissible geometry and explicit effective information |

The two Wishart forms use the same site-contrast likelihood for matching
covariance and distance representations. Passing
[`check_distance_response()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/check_distance_response.md)
does not give an FST ratio estimator a Wishart sampling model. Grouped
covariance should use the coherent `gower` diagonal from landgraph;
`within` is on a different scale. Rare-variant weighting and unequal
group sizes require sensitivity checks.

### What `nu` changes

Wishart point estimates are invariant to rescaling `nu` at the optimum.
Standard errors scale as `1 / sqrt(nu)`, while likelihood-ratio
statistics and the likelihood contribution to information criteria scale
with `nu`. Linkage and shared population history can make effective
information much smaller than the marker count.

Use `terradish_rescale_nu(fit, nu = ...)` to report conclusions over
plausible values. Dividing `nu` by 20 increases standard errors by
`sqrt(20)` without refitting estimates. AIC at nominal marker
information can over-select environmental terms and flexible curves. Use
spatial CV for predictive support and rescaling for inferential
sensitivity.

## Combine IBE and IBR

``` r

# Raster covariates come first; coordinates come second.
environment <- pairwise_endpoint_covariates(covariates, sites)
lonlat <- terra::crds(terra::project(sites, "EPSG:4326"))
local_crs <- sprintf("+proj=aeqd +lat_0=%f +lon_0=%f +datum=WGS84 +units=m",
                     mean(lonlat[, 2]), mean(lonlat[, 1]))
projected_sites <- terra::project(sites, local_crs)
pairwise <- pairwise_covariates(environment,
  geographic_100km = dist(terra::crds(projected_sites)) / 100000)

joint <- terradish(Fst ~ forestcover + altitude, graph,
                   measurement_model = mlpe_covariates(pairwise))
terradish_ibe_ratio(joint)

# The same object can enter a model for a coherent covariance response.
wishart_measurement <- wishart_covariates(pairwise, model = "wishart_covariance")
```

Geographic differences in this example are in units of 100 km. The
IBE:IBR ratio expresses an environmental difference in
resistance-distance units with a joint uncertainty interval. Raw
coefficients are not directly comparable across families. Ratios require
matching transforms and scaling and are undefined when the resistance
coefficient is zero.

Environmental terms can reflect assortative mating, dispersal filtering,
local adaptation, or environmental patterns in site variance. Report
conductance fits with and without pairwise terms because signs can
change. A uniform `~ 1` surface with environmental terms represents
**IBD + IBE**, not IBE alone.

## Model comparison

[`terradish_folds()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_folds.md)
constructs folds;
[`terradish_cv_folds()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_cv_folds.md)
keeps the landscape graph fixed while withholding sites. It accepts
per-formula conductance factories and repeated folds. Reprofiled
nuisance parameters compare conductance formulas under one measurement
model. Set `nuisance = "fixed"` to retain every measurement parameter
from training and score predictive densities when comparing measurement
extensions.

Read success counts first. Failed folds make full totals unavailable,
and rankings use only folds successful for every candidate. Paired
differences and their standard errors are descriptive because folds
share data. Checkpoints reject incompatible input or model changes.

MLPE and Wishart scores do not share a common predictive scale. Within
one Wishart comparison, changing `nu` rescales scores without changing
ranks when the same folds succeed. Likelihood-ratio tests require nested
models, matching responses and graphs, and fixed `nu`. Environmental
Wishart weights need a boundary reference, not an ordinary chi-square
test.

## Prediction and large landscapes

New-landscape prediction reuses fitted log-linear terms, spline knots
and centers, or Gaussian post-smoothing scaling. Apply stored input
scaling with
`scale_covariates(new_rasters, reference = original_scaled_rasters)`
before building a new graph. Slim fits retain covariance and interval
methods but cannot predict after their model closures are removed.

`solver = "auto"` selects AMG above the large-graph threshold regardless
of the number of right-hand sides. AMG iteration counts can increase
with conductance contrast. Experimental parallel derivatives use PSOCK
workers for Hessian and partial solves; AMG and cached CHOLMOD ignore
`cores`.

Cropping changes resistance. One unpublished development check found
increases of 15 to 23% with a two-cell buffer and 1 to 2% with ten
cells. These are case-specific results: compare larger-buffer refits.
Landmark and coarse-raster starts require exact refinement;
[`terradish_grid()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_grid.md)
supports exact evaluation only.
[`terradish_assess_settings()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_assess_settings.md)
is a speed probe, not a convergence or statistical check.

## Experimental features

Directed conductance, hierarchical fields, site-specific drift terms,
pair subsets, Kron reduction, block-CG, and legacy CV remain on the
`experimental` branch. Their unresolved limitations are documented in
that branch’s `EXPERIMENTAL.md`.

``` r

remotes::install_github("wpeterman/terradish@experimental")
```

## Guides

The guides are numbered in reading order. Start with
[`vignette("v01-getting-started", package = "terradish")`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/articles/v01-getting-started.md),
or with
[`vignette("v03-mlpe-pairwise-distance", package = "terradish")`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/articles/v03-mlpe-pairwise-distance.md)
if your data are a pairwise genetic distance matrix such as FST. Open
the collection with `browseVignettes("terradish")`.

| Guide | Question it answers |
|:---|:---|
| `v01-getting-started` | How do I run one complete analysis, from genotypes to a conductance map? |
| `v02-wishart-covariance` | Which genetic covariance response should I model, and is it admissible? |
| `v03-mlpe-pairwise-distance` | How do I fit and read a model of pairwise genetic distances? |
| `v04-model-comparison` | Which candidate model do information criteria and spatial cross-validation support? |
| `v05-categorical-conductance` | How do I fit and interpret land-cover classes? |
| `v06-spline-conductance` | Does a curved association predict better than a straight one? |
| `v07-gaussian-scale-optimization` | Over what neighborhood does a covariate act? |
| `v08-ibe-ibr-workflow` | Do environmental differences matter beyond resistance? |
| `v09-individual-salamanders` | How do individual genotypes reveal a nonlinear resistance response? |
| `v10-simulation-design` | How many sites would a study need? |
| `v11-large-landscapes` | Which solver, storage, and domain settings suit a large raster? |
| `v12-data-generation` | How were the bundled salamander data simulated? |

Changes in each release are listed in `NEWS.md` and in the website
changelog.

## Attribution

Nate Pope developed the sparse graph optimization, reverse-mode
derivatives, MLPE, and generalized Wishart foundations in
[radish](https://github.com/nspope/radish). terradish extends that
framework with terra-native workflows and the supported features above.
Selected deprecated `radish*` wrappers remain; full compatibility with
every historical entry point is not promised.

Report bugs and request features through the [issue
tracker](https://github.com/wpeterman/terradish/issues).

# Package index

## Build the graph

Prepare raster covariates and connect sampling locations to a raster
graph.

- [`scale_covariates()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/scale_covariates.md)
  : Scale raster covariates and retain original-scale metadata
- [`conductance_surface()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/conductance_surface.md)
  : Build the raster graph from covariates and sampling sites
- [`crop_to_focal_buffer()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/crop_to_focal_buffer.md)
  : Crop rasters to a focal-site buffer

## Genetic responses

Construct and check the genetic response. The covariance and distance
constructors are re-exported from landgraph.

- [`reexports`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/reexports.md)
  [`cov_from_biallelic`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/reexports.md)
  [`cov_from_genetic_data`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/reexports.md)
  [`fst_from_biallelic`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/reexports.md)
  [`dist_from_cov`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/reexports.md)
  [`dist_from_biallelic`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/reexports.md)
  : Objects exported from other packages
- [`check_distance_response()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/check_distance_response.md)
  : Check that a squared-distance response is admissible
- [`pca_dist()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/pca_dist.md)
  : Pairwise genetic distances from PCA scores

## Fit and evaluate models

Fit a conductance model by maximum likelihood and work with the fitted
object.

- [`terradish()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish.md)
  : Fit a conductance model by maximum likelihood
- [`print(`*`<terradish>`*`)`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_methods.md)
  [`summary(`*`<terradish>`*`)`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_methods.md)
  [`print(`*`<summary.terradish>`*`)`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_methods.md)
  [`coef(`*`<terradish>`*`)`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_methods.md)
  [`fitted(`*`<terradish>`*`)`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_methods.md)
  [`simulate(`*`<terradish>`*`)`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_methods.md)
  [`anova(`*`<terradish>`*`)`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_methods.md)
  [`logLik(`*`<terradish>`*`)`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_methods.md)
  [`AIC(`*`<terradish>`*`)`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_methods.md)
  [`residuals(`*`<terradish>`*`)`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_methods.md)
  : Print, summarize, compare, and extract from a fitted model
- [`conductance()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/conductance.md)
  : Predict the fitted conductance surface with intervals
- [`terradish_distance()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_distance.md)
  : Resistance distances on a grid of conductance parameters
- [`slim_terradish()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/slim_terradish.md)
  : Shrink a fitted model for storage

## Conductance models

How raster covariates map to cell conductance.

- [`terradish_conductance_model_factory`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_conductance_model_factory.md)
  : Conductance models: the factory interface
- [`loglinear_conductance()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/loglinear_conductance.md)
  : Log-linear conductance model
- [`smooth_loglinear_conductance()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/smooth_loglinear_conductance.md)
  : Log-linear conductance model with spline terms
- [`gaussian_smoothed_loglinear_conductance()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/gaussian_smoothed_loglinear_conductance.md)
  : Log-linear conductance model with estimated Gaussian smoothing
  scales

## Spatial scale

Estimate, profile, and summarize Gaussian smoothing scales.

- [`terradish_scale_optim()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_scale_optim.md)
  : Search raster smoothing scales by refitting the model
- [`gaussian_scale_profile()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/gaussian_scale_profile.md)
  : Profile-likelihood interval for a Gaussian smoothing scale
- [`gaussian_scale_summary()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/gaussian_scale_summary.md)
  : Summarize fitted Gaussian smoothing scales

## Measurement models

How resistance distance or covariance links to the observed genetic
response, including pairwise and site-level environmental covariates.

- [`terradish_measurement_model`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_measurement_model.md)
  : Measurement models: the likelihood interface
- [`mlpe()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/mlpe.md) :
  Maximum likelihood population effects (MLPE) measurement model
- [`mlpe_covariates()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/mlpe_covariates.md)
  : MLPE measurement model with pairwise environmental covariates
- [`mlpe_response_change()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/mlpe_response_change.md)
  : Change in genetic distance across an MLPE pairwise covariate
  contrast
- [`wishart_covariance()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/wishart_covariance.md)
  : Wishart covariance measurement model
- [`wishart_covariates()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/wishart_covariates.md)
  : Wishart measurement model with environmental covariance kernels
- [`generalized_wishart()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/generalized_wishart.md)
  : Generalized Wishart measurement model for squared distances
- [`leastsquares()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/leastsquares.md)
  : Least-squares measurement model
- [`pairwise_covariates()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/pairwise_covariates.md)
  : Combine environmental differences with other pairwise covariates
- [`pairwise_endpoint_covariates()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/pairwise_endpoint_covariates.md)
  : Pairwise environmental differences from site-level covariates
- [`terradish_ibe_ratio()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_ibe_ratio.md)
  : Express environmental effects in resistance-distance units

## Inference and model comparison

Standard errors and intervals, information criteria, and spatial
cross-validation.

- [`vcov(`*`<terradish>`*`)`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_inference.md)
  [`nobs(`*`<terradish>`*`)`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_inference.md)
  [`confint(`*`<terradish>`*`)`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_inference.md)
  : Standard errors and confidence intervals for conductance parameters
- [`terradish_rescale_nu()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_rescale_nu.md)
  : Rescale the effective information in a Wishart fit
- [`aic_table()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/aic_table.md)
  : Rank fitted models by AIC, AICc, or BIC
- [`terradish_folds()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_folds.md)
  : Assign sampling sites to cross-validation folds
- [`terradish_cv_folds()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_cv_folds.md)
  [`print(`*`<terradish_cv_folds>`*`)`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_cv_folds.md)
  : Spatial cross-validation of conductance formulas on a fixed graph

## Plotting

Diagnostic and interpretive plots of a fitted model.

- [`plot(`*`<terradish>`*`)`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/plot.terradish.md)
  : Plot a fitted model: fit, surface, marginal curves, and smoothing
  kernels

Simulate covariance responses and assess parameter recovery.

  : Simulate genetic covariance matrices from a known conductance
  surface
- [`covariance_response_power()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/covariance_response_power.md)
  : Simulation-based power and parameter recovery for sampling designs
- [`print(`*`<terradish_covariance_power>`*`)`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/print.terradish_covariance_power.md)
  : Print and read a power assessment

## Large landscapes and solver settings

Solver benchmarks and speed settings for large rasters.

- [`terradish_assess_settings()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_assess_settings.md)
  : Recommend optimizer and solver settings for a data set
- [`print(`*`<terradish_setting_assessment>`*`)`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/print.terradish_setting_assessment.md)
  : Print and read a settings assessment
- [`terradish_solver_benchmark()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_solver_benchmark.md)
  : Benchmark sparse Cholesky solver settings on a graph

## Optimizer controls

Tuning for the Newton-type optimizers and their line searches.

- [`NewtonRaphsonControl()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/NewtonRaphsonControl.md)
  : Control settings for the Newton and BFGS optimizers
- [`ArmijoControl()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/ArmijoControl.md)
  : Control settings for Armijo backtracking line search
- [`HagerZhangControl()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/HagerZhangControl.md)
  : Control settings for Hager-Zhang line search

Bundled example data used in the help pages and guides.

  : Simulated Ohio forest-pond SNP and microsatellite data

  : Simulated individual salamander genotypes and resistance analyses
- [`melip`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/melip.md) :
  Melipona stingless bee landscape and FST example data

Names kept from the radish package and their terradish replacements.

## Low-level tools

Direct likelihood evaluation and small helpers. Most analyses do not
need these.

- [`terradish_grid()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_grid.md)
  : Profile likelihood on a grid of conductance parameters
- [`terradish_algorithm()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/terradish_algorithm.md)
  : Low-level likelihood and derivatives at one parameter value
- [`lower()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/lower.md)
  : Extract the strict lower triangle of a matrix
- [`scale_to_0_1()`](https://wpeterman.github.io/terradish/reference/scale_to_0_1.md)
  : Rescale values to the unit interval

Choose and check the genetic quantity the model explains: an
allele-frequency covariance with a Wishart likelihood, or a pairwise
genetic distance with MLPE.

Beyond a linear term: land-cover classes, curved associations, and the
